sources.entry: Tinode - Instant messaging platform. Backend in Go. Clients: Swift iOS, Java Android, JS webapp, scriptable command line; chatbots. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: Tinode is a self-hostable instant messaging server written in Go, with native Android, iOS and web clients and gRPC/JSON client bindings for many languages, positioned as a federated-style alternative to XMPP.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a full instant messaging stack: a pure Go backend plus Android (Java), iOS (Swift) and web (ReactJS) clients. Wire transport is JSON over websocket (long polling also available) or protobuf over gRPC. It supports one-on-one and group chats, channels with read-only subscribers, voice and video calls, file and image attachments, message editing, replies, forwarding, and presence and typing notifications. Administration features include granular permissions, custom authentication backends, server-side blocking, anonymous users, plugins, and a scriptable command-line tool. Storage backends include MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB and RethinkDB, with media stored on the local file system or Amazon S3.
use_cases: building chatbots on a messaging API
customer tech support chat with anonymous users
group messaging and channels for an organization
running a private messenger with my own database
how_to_run: See the general installation instructions or the Docker-specific instructions referenced in the README
Read the configuration instructions in the tinode.conf file
Alternatively, use one of the public cloud services mentioned in the README
notable: Explicitly positioned as a replacement for XMPP, not XMPP-compatible
Client bindings for JavaScript, Java, Swift, and gRPC languages including C++, C#, Go, Python, PHP and Ruby
Sandbox demo with test accounts and a chatbot user
Pluggable database adapters and media handlers
Supports both JSON and protobuf wire protocols
caveats: README describes the software as beta-quality, feature-complete and stable but possibly with bugs or missing features
Federation is only planned, not implemented; end-to-end encryption and message encryption at rest are also planned
RethinkDB support is deprecated and will be dropped in 2027
Arango and DynamoDB adapters are listed as outdated
summary.license: GPL-3.0 (server); client libraries are Apache 2.0 per the README
